correctness.rationale: For A an automorphism has f -> ue+tf, e -> t^2 e by preservation of [f,f], and tensor pushforward has weight t^4/t=t^3 on the parameter. For B use g=f-e: the only nonzero bracket is [g,e]=e, so preservation of Ke and the brackets forces e -> te and g -> g. Family I has delta(e)=0 and delta(g)=(A_0+gamma) e⊗e+gamma e⊗g, so the weights are 2 and 1, respectively. For gamma nonzero normalize uniquely to gamma=1; for gamma zero take square classes of the first coefficient. Family II has only delta(e)=lambda(e⊗g-g⊗e), so its input and output transformations cancel. Its nonzero members cannot lie in family I since the derived line has nonzero cobracket there. These arguments have no exceptional characteristic. Source witness formulas and the defining coalgebra and compatibility identities are integral polynomial formulas; the parameter identities holding over the reals are integral polynomial identities and specialize to every field. This argument does not transfer real-field completeness. A and B differ in nilpotence. Finite-field multiplicative cyclicity gives the gcd counts, and the raw reduced locus is a disjoint union of an affine line and a plane and line meeting at the origin. Thus over extensions its count is q^(2m)+2q^m-1 and the exponential generating definition of zeta gives the stated rational function, not the zeta of the orbit set. Read VERIFICATION.md and artifacts/verify.py and compared artifacts/verify_output.txt against the formulas; no uploaded code was run. The proof applies to arbitrary fields independently of the five retained prime-field enumerations.

value.rationale: The source tables pose a natural classification problem after forgetting redundant witnesses. The solution distinguishes genuinely different continuous moduli and arithmetic square/cube classes, and gives exact isomorphism counts over all finite fields. This is useful even though it intentionally does not classify all positive-characteristic triangular structures.
